result.title: Temporal Leakage Distorts the TGB Node Affinity Leaderboard: A Point-in-Time Audit
result.summary: Node affinity prediction in the Temporal Graph Benchmark (TGB) asks how a node's future interactions will be distributed over other nodes. On this task, methods that reuse past ground-truth labels often outperform temporal graph neural networks, and the state of the art builds on them. Such comparisons assume a point-in-time correct evaluation, in which a model receives only information available at prediction time. Drawing on as-of joins and bitemporal databases, we formalize this requirement by distinguishing when a label must be predicted, its query time, from when it is fully determined, its availability time, and we audit the four TGB node affinity datasets and their evaluation loop with model-agnostic tools. None of the four meets it. On three datasets, each label summarizes a single day about five days after its timestamp, not the documented following week, yet the loop feeds it back right after that timestamp; on the fourth, the loop processes the edges from which each label is computed before predicting it. Under a drop-in leakage-free protocol, every method whose inputs leak loses up to 17% of its NDCG@10, the advantage of past labels over the interaction stream nearly vanishes or reverses, and both the best configuration of the state of the art and the rankings change; a blend of training-free long-memory statistics, with weights fit on validation data, matches or exceeds the state of the art under both protocols. Point-in-time correctness should therefore be built into benchmarks, and our tools carry over to other benchmarks whose labels aggregate event streams over time windows.

AI.brief_summary: 该文审计 Temporal Graph Benchmark 的节点亲和度任务，区分标签的「查询时间」与「可用时间」，发现四个数据集及其评测循环均存在时间泄漏，并给出无泄漏协议：泄漏方法 NDCG@10 最多下降 17%，排名与最优配置改变。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「按时间点正确、区分预测时点与信息可用时点」的审计框架，可能可供核查 LVR/VLM 推理评测中视觉证据是否在决策时点确实可得、是否存在答案或未来信息泄漏；与 latent 状态生成本身无直接关系。
